claims.text: Cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a naturally occurring coarse lamellar composite microstructure.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure that inherits the cast lamellar structure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The required processing route specifically combines controlled hot rolling, cold rolling, and optimized annealing.
The processing partially recrystallizes the alloy while retaining ultrafine inherited lamellae.
The processed alloy exhibits nanoscale and microscale hierarchical heterogeneity associated with a duplex structure.
The hierarchical structural heterogeneity arises at least partly from phase decomposition.
Processing temperature, strain rate, and annealing duration must be carefully selected to stabilize the duplex microstructure.
The benefits apply only within a particular window of AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic compositions.
Excessive annealing can cause complete recrystallization or grain growth, preventing formation of the beneficial duplex structure.
The inherited hierarchical structure produces a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The inherited structure produces a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Retained lamellar regions act as in situ reinforcements.
The retained lamellae enhance work hardening and delay shear localization.
Grain refinement increases yield strength while improving ductility.
Hierarchical phase load-sharing increases the effective Young's modulus.
The tailored microstructure improves the strength-ductility synergy relative to previously reported reinforcement approaches.
The treatment increases yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional processing.
The treatment maintains or improves ductility relative to conventional processing.
The treatment increases Young's modulus by approximately 20%.
The treatment enhances fracture resistance by delaying crack propagation under fatigue or impact loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says ductility is boosted, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to remain similar.

The predicted outcome allows similar ductility, but the falsification rule appears to require ductility, along with every other listed property, to be statistically significantly higher by roughly 5–10% or more.
